Before you flip this switch this afternoon, the "one-line config change" framing undersells what's actually changing here — and the AcmeCo detail you flagged is the reason why.

**This isn't just a billing swap.** OpenAI's Enterprise tier and the standard API operate under different contractual terms: data retention windows, zero-retention options, DPA terms, audit rights, and security commitments (SOC2 scope, etc.) typically differ between an Enterprise agreement and the self-serve API ToS. Moving the bot means every diff it processes — including AcmeCo's proprietary code from the private fork — will be governed by whatever data handling terms apply to the new plan, not the ones your org negotiated under Enterprise.

**The AcmeCo angle is the real risk.** If your support contract with AcmeCo includes any language about how their code/data is handled by third-party tooling (security certifications, data residency, retention limits, "enterprise-grade" vendor requirements, no-subprocessor clauses, etc.), routing their diffs through a different OpenAI plan could put you in breach even though the model and prompts are identical. This is a legal/contract question, not an engineering one, and it's not something Priya's output-quality comparison would have surfaced — that test only validated review quality, not data handling terms.

**Recommendation:** before merging, get whoever owns the AcmeCo relationship (legal or account owner) to confirm the standard API's data terms satisfy the support contract's obligations — or exclude the AcmeCo fork from the bot until that's confirmed. Don't let the finance deadline drive this without that sign-off; a same-day contract breach costs a lot more than a month of Enterprise pricing.
